bibliography.title: Implant Strength Contributes to the Osseointegration Strength of Porous Metallic Materials
bibliography.authors: Mathey E, Pelletier MH, Walsh WR, Gall K, Carpenter D.
bibliography.publication_type: Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't; research-article; Research Support, U.S. Gov't, Non-P.H.S.; Journal Article; Research Support, N.I.H., Extramural

study.research_problem: Porous implants are often optimized for low stiffness and load sharing, but high porosity also lowers strength and may cause implant/bone plastic collapse before a mechanically strong osseointegrated interface develops.
study.exact_gap: Elastic or empty-lattice analyses do not explain why very porous gyroid implants can share load yet show lower push-out strength; a multimaterial failure-capable model linked to in-vivo push-out data was needed.
study.objective_or_hypothesis: Calibrate a bone–implant push-out FE model on the solid group, test whether it predicts 50–90% porosity trends, and use component plasticity/load sharing to explain how porosity changes assembly strength.
study.study_design: Nonlinear multimaterial FE study reusing 12-week ovine bicortical push-out experiments (n=8/group): mesh convergence, staged constitutive-model development, two-parameter calibration on the 0% group, comparison with porous groups, and local plasticity/load-sharing analysis.
study.sample_or_model: 6-mm Ti gyroid implants at 0, 50, 60, 70, 80, and 90% porosity; idealized fully filled homogeneous isotropic ingrown bone, cortical bone block, rigid indenter, tied bone–implant interface, and prior ovine push-out curves.
comparators: FE predictions versus experimental group means/curves
Low versus high global force load sharing
method_spine: Replicate push-out geometry and verify mesh convergence for the 70% model.
Add nonlinear plastic behavior component by component to identify necessary failure physics.
Fit ingrown-bone ash density and frame-compliance correction to the solid experimental group.
Apply fixed calibration to 50–90% groups and compare stiffness/0.5-mm force trends.
Interrogate component forces, stresses, and plastic zones across load levels.

verification: Mesh refinement changed stiffness <3% and 0.5-mm force <2.5% for the 70% model, then convergence was assumed for other porosities (S003:C02-S003:C03).
calibration: Ingrown-bone ash density and test-frame compliance were fitted to maximum force and stiffness of the 0% experimental group (S006:C01-S006:C02).
validation: The 50–90% experimental groups were not used for parameter fitting and provide a conditional porosity holdout with high trend correlations, but they come from the same study/timepoint and the model systematically overpredicts values (S008:C03-S008:C05; S010:C01-S010:C03).
sensitivity: Mesh and constitutive plasticity inclusion are examined; bone fill, tie/contact, ash density, geometry imperfection, and other parameter uncertainties are not systematically varied.
application_prediction: The reported 60–70% favorable range applies only to this gyroid, size, material, 12-week ovine ingrowth approximation, and push-out loading (S014:C01).

primary_outcomes: Plasticity in ingrown bone and implant is required to reproduce yield/post-yield trends; elastic-only models miss failure behavior (S008:C01-S008:C02; S009:C01-S009:C02).
Porous-group FE stiffness and 0.5-mm force trends correlate strongly with experimental means (r2 0.98 and 0.97), while predictions remain systematically high (S008:C03-S008:C05).
Higher porosity increases bone load share, but at 80–90% the implant plastically collapses and drives high local bone stress/plasticity at lower global force (S008:C06-S008:C10).
50–70% designs have similar load-sharing fractions over much of the load range, showing that lower stiffness alone is not a sufficient optimization objective (S011:C01-S011:C03).
study.highest_evidence_level_reached: Mechanistically interpretable FE prediction with within-study experimental holdout across porosity at one ovine time point; no independent device/clinical validation.

argument_map.central_claim: Porous implant design must jointly consider stiffness, strength, and load-dependent plasticity because excessive porosity can improve low-load sharing yet reduce construct strength through implant collapse and secondary bone overloading.
data: Staged material models show that component plasticity changes global response (S008:C01-S008:C02).
Calibrated models reproduce porous-group trends but overpredict magnitudes (S008:C03-S008:C05).
Load-share curves and plastic-zone maps connect high porosity to implant and bone yield (S008:C06-S008:C10).
argument_map.warrant: A design is mechanically favorable only if it transfers useful load to bone without entering a low-strength regime that creates damaging local stresses before global failure.
backing: Experimental push-out trends provide a conditional check on the modeled porosity ranking (S008:C03-S008:C05).
argument_map.qualifier: For the current gyroid, geometry, early ovine ingrowth, and push-out load case.
rebuttals_or_boundaries: The model assumes complete homogeneous bone fill and perfect bonding (S010:C02).
The 0% group supplies two fitted quantities, so it is calibration rather than validation (S006:C01-S006:C02).
Porous comparisons are same-study holdouts, not an external dataset.
Long-term remodeling, fatigue, imperfect as-built geometry, and biological ingrowth are outside the model (S014:C01).

measured: Prior ovine push-out force–displacement curves and printed-solid titanium tensile data are experimental inputs/comparators (S003:C01; S005:C01; S008:C03).
predicted: FE stiffness, 0.5-mm force, load sharing, component stress, and plastic strain for all assemblies are predictions (S007:C01-S008:C10).
inferred: Implant collapse is inferred as the mechanism for low high-porosity assembly strength from convergent model maps and experimental trends (S008:C08-S010:C01).
A 60–70% range is inferred as favorable for this setup, not a universal biological optimum (S010:C01; S014:C01).
Low bone stress in the 50% model is suggested to be inadequate for growth without a remodeling measurement (S012:C02).
recommended: Optimize stiffness and strength together and test porosity effects on long-term bone regeneration/mineralization (S012:C01-S013:C01).
proxy_to_outcome_bridges: Push-out strength measures fixation at 12 weeks, not long-term osseointegration or clinical survival.
Modeled bone stress/load share is a mechanobiological proxy, not measured remodeling.
Trend correlation does not establish unbiased absolute prediction.
overclaim_risks: The abstract calls the model validated without distinguishing solid-group calibration from porous same-study holdout (S001:C01).
'Optimal porosity 60–70%' can be misread as universal despite explicit current-structure/loading limits (S001:C01; S014:C01).
Perfect fill/tie create a best-case model that systematically overpredicts force (S008:C04-S010:C03).

section_moves.move: Disclose calibration targets and holdout groups
section_moves.execution: The exact solid-group quantities used to fit bone density and frame compliance are stated before fixed parameters are applied to porous groups (S006:C01-S006:C02).
section_moves.transferable_principle: Name every fitted parameter, target dataset, and held-out comparison; do not call calibration data validation.
section_moves.failure_mode: A fully external validation set and uncertainty propagation are absent.

section_moves.move: Report both agreement and systematic bias
section_moves.execution: High porosity-trend correlations are presented alongside consistent absolute overprediction and experimental variability (S008:C03-S008:C05).
section_moves.transferable_principle: A validation paragraph should report direction/magnitude of bias, not only correlation or visual overlap.
section_moves.failure_mode: Few porosity levels make r2 unstable and do not quantify prediction error intervals.

section_moves.move: Replace single-point stiffness reasoning with a load-dependent failure mechanism
section_moves.execution: The paper shows how load sharing changes with global force and how implant strength reverses the apparent benefit at high porosity (S011:C01-S012:C02).
section_moves.transferable_principle: For nonlinear implants, discuss load sharing as a trajectory across load and failure, linking global metrics to local component states.
section_moves.failure_mode: Biological consequences remain inferred from mechanical fields.

author_reported: Ideal geometry, homogeneous full bone fill, perfect interface bonding, and equal component heights contribute to overprediction (S010:C02-S010:C03).
Animal/surgical variation and a single 12-week time point limit long-term inference; results apply to the current gyroid (S014:C01).
reader_identified: Convergence is demonstrated for one porosity and assumed for others.
No material/contact/bone-fill probabilistic sensitivity or as-built CT geometry.
Same-study porous groups are useful holdouts but not independent external validation.
Tie contact precludes interfacial debond/slip, central to push-out failure.
Correlation across few group means can appear strong despite systematic bias.
likely_bias_direction: Perfect fill/tie and ideal geometry bias strength predictions upward.
Calibration on the solid group may favor trends sharing the same experimental system.
Calling a local range optimal biases scope toward universality.
limitations.scope_boundary: The model supports a mechanical explanation and porosity trend for a 6-mm gyroid in a 12-week ovine push-out setup; it does not define a universal lattice optimum or validate long-term biological/clinical osseointegration.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Distinguish numerical verification, parameter calibration, same-study holdout comparison, and independent validation in FE writing.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Methods, validation Results, abstract, and limitations.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: High r2 on group means does not erase calibration overlap, systematic bias, or missing external validation.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Write porous-implant optimization as stiffness–strength–plasticity–load-sharing trade-offs across load, not as modulus matching alone.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Design rationale, Results, and mechanism Discussion.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Mechanical fields require a separate biological link before claiming remodeling or long-term osseointegration.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Constrain every reported optimum by architecture, dimensions, material state, load case, species, and time point.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Use 'favorable within the tested design space' unless external architectures and conditions support universality.

critical_weaknesses: Limited uncertainty/sensitivity and one-timepoint same-study holdout.

summary_zh: 本文提供了非常可迁移的 FE 写作范式：网格收敛是 verification；用 0% 实心组拟合骨密度和机架顺应性是 calibration；50–90% 组是同一实验中的按孔隙率留出比较；模型仍系统性高估绝对值。力学结论也从“降低刚度”升级为刚度–强度–塑性–载荷分担随载荷演化的联合问题。60–70% 只能写成当前 gyroid、尺寸、12 周羊模型和 push-out 工况内的有利区间。
reader_notes: 已阅读全文全部非参考文献章节。
实验数据来自既往羊模型；本文的新增核心是 FE 与机制解释。
